sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

content.thinking:
Looking at the thigh image, I can see the femur with its cortex as a dark ring and marrow of intermediate signal. There's a bright crescent-shaped mass wrapped around the lateral side of the femur, likely the tumor, with marker points 589, 545, and 564 positioned along this bright region and near the bone's dark cortical edge.

Mapping the coordinates across panels, I confirm 589 at the left panel's x≈507, y≈354 falls right within the bright crescent spanning roughly x 480-530, y 280-420. That makes 589 the correct choice.

content.text:
Mark 589 sits in the bright crescent of abnormal T2 signal that wraps around the femur on the patient's left side (image right), which I take to be the tumor. Marks 564 and 545 are close to it but fall nearer the bone edge and the outer margin of the bright region. Mark 589 is the one that lies within the mass.

ANSWER: 589
